So I have two very awesome, but sometimes rambunctious cats. I am in the process of moving into a new place and the entrance/door situation is problematic. They've been fine with regular entrances for a long time; however, this place has no AC and it relies on using the secondary metal screen door outside of the front door for airflow during the summer.

This becomes a problem with the cats because it will become impossible to open the door some days without them getting out if they get used to that door being used as a screen.

Anyways, I'm thinking about building and installing a secondary door at the end of the entry way so we can be certain the cats won't be able to run out. The entry way [looks like this](https://i.sli.mg/dVJ6Q2.jpg). It's approximately 46 inches wide, 7.5 feet tall and has about 2.5 inches of depth available.

I was thinking about using a slatted wood design for both the door and the border so it wouldn't restrict airflow to the rest of the room...and it would also give an open view to the living room when you enter.

Anyone have any thoughts, experiences or ideas to share for this endeavor? I've never built anything like a door, door frame or slatted/open design before so I'm open to ideas, stories or opinions!
Looking to build an indoor door. Ideas wanted!

I would think having to deal with two doors, especially when coming in and out with loads of groceries, etc. would be a pain.
What about a gate that only swings inward (so the cats can't push it to get towards the front door)...Something you could push with your leg if your arms were full? It would have to either be tall enough that the cats couldn't jump over it and/or have something on it that would discourage them from doing so.

That's a pretty good idea to have a gate that only opens from one side. Thanks! The main issue is that they can easily jump 4-5 feet, so if it's something that has to be that high, then might as well go the extra two feet to the ceiling.

Although I don't want to look like a drug dealer with a cage entrance.

If you want a do it yourself solution, I would look at using something like garden trellis panels.you can get them made from wood, metal or PVC. They are paintable and with a little cutting you can make them fit your entrance. If you get like 3 narrow ones with a couple of piano hinges, you could make something blike a changing screen that easily stores flat against the wall when you don't need it.
Awesome idea. This is really practical as well. I'll look into something like this over the weekend
It may not be perfect, but I figured if it was a rental you may want something that doesn't require putting holes in the Wal or adding permanent structures. I Hope you find simething cool, good luck.
